title: Completing Categorical Lawvere: The Sorry Root Cause
content: This file resolves 2 sorries in the parent `cantor-diagonalization-oq-03-oq-01`. The **root cause**: the parent's hypothesis used `sorry : C.Pt (C.exp A B)` — a constant term — where a **function** `e a : C.Pt (C.exp A B)` (depending on `a : C.Pt A`) was needed. The fix: make `e : C.Pt A → C.Pt (C.exp A B)` an explicit parameter. The proof body then trivially reduces to `lawvere_abstract` via an `EvalStructure`.
mathContext: **Lawvere's fixed-point theorem** (1969): in any cartesian closed category, if $e: A \to B^A$ is a point-surjection (every $f: A \to B$ factors through $\text{ev} \circ e$), then every endomorphism $B \to B$ has a fixed point. This unifies: Cantor ($B = \Omega$, $f = \neg$), Russell's paradox, the halting problem, and Gödel's first incompleteness theorem. The challenge: Mathlib doesn't have full CCC/topos machinery, requiring an abstract intermediate layer (`EvalStructure`).

title: EvalStructure and lawvere_abstract: The Core Diagonal Argument
content: **EvalStructure**: a structure with `Ob : Type*`, `Val : Type*`, `eval : Ob → Ob → Val` — models $\text{ev}: B^A \times A \to B$ at global elements. **IsPointSurjective**: every $g: \text{Ob} \to \text{Val}$ is representable: $\exists a, \forall x, \text{eval}(a, x) = g(x)$. **lawvere_abstract** (3 lines): if E is point-surjective, every $f: \text{Val} \to \text{Val}$ has a fixed point. Proof: get $a_0$ representing $a \mapsto f(\text{eval}(a,a))$; then $\text{eval}(a_0, a_0) = f(\text{eval}(a_0, a_0))$.
mathContext: The proof is the **diagonal construction**: the function $g(a) = f(\text{eval}(a, a))$ is representable by some $a_0$. Substituting $a = a_0$: $\text{eval}(a_0, a_0) = g(a_0) = f(\text{eval}(a_0, a_0))$. So $v = \text{eval}(a_0, a_0)$ is a fixed point. In Lean: `obtain ⟨a₀, ha₀⟩ := hE (fun a => f (E.eval a a))` extracts $a_0$, then `exact ⟨E.eval a₀ a₀, (ha₀ a₀).symm⟩` packages the fixed point. The `.symm` flips the direction of the equality.

title: CategoricalEval Structure: CCC Without Topos Machinery
content: **CategoricalEval**: a structure abstracting a cartesian closed category at the level of global elements: `Obj`, `Hom`, `exp` (exponential object), `Pt` (global elements), `apply` (evaluation map $\text{ev}$), `ptSurj` (point-surjectivity criterion). **HasFixedPoint**: $\exists b, f(b) = b$. The `ptSurj` field is a placeholder — the actual surjectivity condition is stated as a parameter in theorems.
mathContext: In a CCC, the **exponential** $B^A$ is characterized by $\text{Hom}(C, B^A) \cong \text{Hom}(C \times A, B)$. Global elements = morphisms from the terminal object $1$: $\text{Pt}(A) = \text{Hom}(1, A)$. The **evaluation map** $\text{ev}: B^A \times A \to B$ at global elements: $\text{apply}: \text{Pt}(B^A) \to \text{Pt}(A) \to \text{Pt}(B)$. This structure is inhabited by `typeUniverse`: objects = types, Hom = functions, exp A B = A → B, Pt = id, apply = function application.

title: lawvere_categorical (Fixed): EvalStructure as the Bridge
content: **lawvere_categorical** (corrected, 0 sorries): Given `C : CategoricalEval`, `e : C.Pt A → C.Pt (C.exp A B)` (explicit), and `hSurj`: every $g: \text{Pt}(A) \to \text{Pt}(B)$ factors through `e`, every $f: \text{Pt}(B) \to \text{Pt}(B)$ has a fixed point. Proof: define `E : EvalStructure` with `eval a x = C.apply (e a) x`; note `hSurj = E.IsPointSurjective`; apply `lawvere_abstract`.
mathContext: The `let E : EvalStructure` construction defines the bridge: `Ob = C.Pt A`, `Val = C.Pt B`, `eval = fun a x => C.apply (e a) x`. The surjectivity `hSurj` directly matches `E.IsPointSurjective` since `E.eval a x = C.apply (e a) x`. So `have hE : E.IsPointSurjective := hSurj` is definitional. Then `exact lawvere_abstract E hE f`. The entire proof body after fixing the sorry is **4 lines**. The parent's sorry arose because `e` was missing — the hypothesis `C.apply (sorry) x = g x` used a constant sorry where `e a` was needed.
prerequisites: explicit e : Pt A → Pt(exp A B)

title: typeUniverse Instance and Categorical Cantor's Theorem
content: **typeUniverse**: the `CategoricalEval` where objects = types, exp = function type, apply = function application. **categorical_cantor**: for any `e : A → A → Prop`, `e` is not point-surjective in the type-universe CCC. The function $g(a) = \neg e(a)(a)$ is not representable, because representing it would give $e(a_0)(a_0) = \neg e(a_0)(a_0)$, a contradiction.

title: Connection: Categorical → Type-Theoretic Lawvere
content: **categorical_specializes_to_type_theoretic**: For `e : A → A → B` with `Function.Surjective e`, every `f : B → B` has a fixed point. Proved by building `C : CategoricalEval` from type universe, translating `Function.Surjective e` to `hSurj` via `congr_fun`, and applying `lawvere_categorical`. This bridges the abstract categorical theorem to the elementary type-theoretic version.
mathContext: Translation: `Function.Surjective e` says $\forall g: A \to B, \exists a, e(a) = g$. The categorical `hSurj` says $\forall g, \exists a, \forall x, e(a)(x) = g(x)$. These are **propositionally equal**: from $e(a_0) = g$ (function equality), `congr_fun ha₀ x` extracts $e(a_0)(x) = g(x)$. The `let C` construction is the same type-universe structure as `typeUniverse`. After the proof, `#check` statements verify all four main theorems are registered.
